julia: Heads-up — when bringing up light-rerank-v2 on webqa-v3 holdout I see a small but consistent nDCG@10 dip (~0.022) vs our current prod reranker. MRR basically flat. Not sure if it's dataset sampling, sample_weighting, or an ordering artifact. Anyone free to eyeball quick?
samir: can you paste the exact numbers and the eval config you used? dataset / split / seed?
julia: sure — quick paste: nDCG@10: prod=0.612, light-rerank-v2=0.590 (delta -0.022). MRR@10: prod=0.276, light-rerank-v2=0.274. Dataset: webqa-v3.holdout (5k queries), seed=42, shard=3. Eval config snippet: ```json
{
  "model": "light-rerank-v2",
  "quant": "int8-hybrid",
  "sample_weighting": true,
  "doc_order": "original",
  "batch_size": 64
}
```
I also ran float32 briefly and saw more parity with prod but hadn't finished that run.
anya: two quick hypotheses: 1) sample_weighting biasing training objective toward long docs, which hurts short-query ndcg; 2) anchor/doc ordering (we ingest passages in canonical order) — some models are sensitive to doc interleaving. Have you checked per-query-length slices? :thinking:
kevin: and check whether our preprocessing tokenization differs between the two model build artifacts (tokenizer vocab/normalization). small shifts can flip near-ties.
samir: can you share a couple of example queries where the ranker flipped? might be useful to inspect rescores.
julia: dropping two example qids (anonymized): qid: 12345 (short), qid: 67890 (long). For 12345 prod top3: [A,B,C], light-rerank-v2 top3: [B,A,C] — so swap A/B. For 67890 we see reordering of long passages where sample_weighting seems to upweight longer doc relevance.
anya: ok let's run an ablation matrix: (A) sample_weighting on/off, (B) doc_order original/shuffled, (C) quant int8/float32. 2x2x2 = 8 runs, 5k queries each should be fine. I can help queue them.
julia: that sounds good. command I'll use (local eval harness): ```bash
python eval/harness.py \--dataset webqa-v3.holdout \--model light-rerank-v2 \--queries 5000 \--seed 42 \--output /tmp/eval_runs/run_<tag>.json
```
I'll loop over flags.
samir: for reproducibility include `--shuffle-seed` for shuffled doc order. also capture `--tokenizer-config` path in metadata so we can compare token counts.
kevin: also capture tie-breaker behavior (stable sort vs random). add `--tie-break stable` and log topk scores for ties.
eval-bot: eval run created: id=run_2026032101, queued by julia, 8 jobs scheduled. ETA ~18m.
julia: nice, I'll paste results here when they finish. earliest plan: compare ndcg by query-length buckets (<=8 tokens, 9-32, >32) and by candidate-length to verify sample_weight skew.
anya: if sample_weighting is the culprit we should try a quick weighted ablation: `sample_weighting: trimmed` (cap weight by 3) to see monotonic effects.
samir: agree. if quantization interacts, we might see ordering differences only in int8 path — keep logs for kv-cache usage and any dequant rounding warnings.
kevin: ping me if float32 run shows parity with prod — if so we can suspect int8 kernel numeric drift and prioritize a tiny retrain / calibration.
julia: running now. i'll post run ids and paste quick diff table once available. thanks all :thumbsup:
(eval-bot will post results)
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job1 complete (sample_weight:on, doc_order:original, quant:int8) — nDCG@10=0.590; MRR=0.274.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job2 complete (sample_weight:on, doc_order:original, quant:float32) — nDCG@10=0.606; MRR=0.276.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job3 complete (sample_weight:off, doc_order:original, quant:int8) — nDCG@10=0.605; MRR=0.275.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job4 complete (sample_weight:off, doc_order:original, quant:float32) — nDCG@10=0.611; MRR=0.276.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job5 complete (sample_weight:on, doc_order:shuffled, quant:int8) — nDCG@10=0.591; MRR=0.274.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job6 complete (sample_weight:on, doc_order:shuffled, quant:float32) — nDCG@10=0.607; MRR=0.276.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job7 complete (sample_weight:off, doc_order:shuffled, quant:int8) — nDCG@10=0.606; MRR=0.275.
eval-bot: run_2026032101.job8 complete (sample_weight:off, doc_order:shuffled, quant:float32) — nDCG@10=0.612; MRR=0.276.
julia: preliminary takeaway: int8 path + sample_weight:on shows largest drop. switching off sample_weight largely recovers ndcg even for int8. doc_order shuffle had minor effect. float32 consistently close to prod.
anya: so root cause likely interaction between sample weighting and quantization (numeric sensitivity). next steps: 1) reproduce on a larger holdout (20k), 2) try trimmed weighting (cap) and soft-label smoothing during training, 3) verify tokenization parity for those qids.
samir: +1. also log per-candidate score distributions to see if quantization compresses score spread.
julia: I'll spin up the 20k runs and do trimmed-weight experiment. Will open a short PR to add the `sample_weight: capped` option in the eval harness so we can iterate faster.
kevin: nice triage. if you want I can help run a micro-calibration pass on int8 kernels to see if we can make them less sensitive.
julia: please do — will DM details. closing in thread for now, will post results. :wave:
